document_title: League City Proposition A, the November 3rd vote on Flock cameras
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
A "nonbinding" no would reach League City's cameras.

The word is the ballot's. On Harris County's sample ballot, Proposition A asks "As a nonbinding statement of voter preference" whether police should keep the fixed plate reader cameras. The council added the word on August 11th. League City lies in Galveston and Harris counties. Harris County vote centers take voters from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3rd.

The council's own record goes further. On October 13th it passed Resolution No. 2026-185 by 8 to 0. It directs removal of the fixed cameras if a majority rejects their continued use. Mayor Nick Long told the council "there's no second vote needed," the Tribune reported.

By the Tribune's account Long put the start of bagging at 72 hours after certification. If a majority votes no Tuesday, when will the count be certified?

S1.headline: League City votes Tuesday on its Flock cameras
S1.body: Proposition A asks whether police keep plate reader cameras at fixed locations on public roadways. The Tribune reports it is the first such vote in Texas. Drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: 42 cameras in 2022, then 70

S3.headline: 70 leased, 55 on the roads
S3.body: The 2023 lease covers 70 cameras. Proposition A asks about 55 along public roads, the Tribune reported. A lease and a road count measure different things. Drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: More than 400 agencies can look
S4.body: All but the FBI are in Texas. The mayor said six League City officers have access. Two must work together to scan the data. Each line is from the Tribune's reporting. One white marker is one agency, one amber marker one officer. Drawn to illustrate.

S5.headline: Seven For, seven For, then eight
S5.body: December 12th, 2023, the lease. August 11th, the election order, one member absent. October 13th, a resolution on the cameras. No member on the three rolls voted against. One bar is one recorded vote. Drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: The ballot calls itself nonbinding
S6.body: Harris County's sample ballot reads "As a nonbinding statement of voter preference, should the League City Police Department continue using automated license plate reader cameras at fixed locations on public roadways for law enforcement purposes?" The council added the word on August 11th. Drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: If voters say no, removal is already directed
S7.body: Resolution No. 2026-185 passed on October 13th with every member on the roll voting For. "There's no second vote needed," Mayor Nick Long said, the Tribune reported. Drawn to illustrate.
